Earnings-quality view: the issuer bridge reconciles, but creditor-accepted quality-adjusted EBITDA remains Not calculable because material normalisation treatments are unresolved. FY2024 ordinary EBITDA is 3,813 and EBITDA As Defined is 4,173. The 360 signed adjustment uplift is not demonstrated sustainable cash earning power. All four annual categories occurred in FY2022 and FY2023; current-quarter acquisition and compensation adjustments continue, while Other is a negative (64). FY2024 OCF conversion is 53.63% on ordinary EBITDA and 49.01% on As Defined. Recurrence challenges blanket one-off acceptance, not the transcription or existence of the charges.

Adjusted-debt view: known-item analytical debt subtotal is 25,002 at September 30, 2024, versus CP-1 carrying debt of 24,880. It includes operating leases 62, gross recognised pension liabilities 19 without cross-plan asset netting, and environmental remediation reserves 41. Finance leases and securitization are already included. This explicitly incomplete subtotal excludes unresolved claims and treats declared dividends as liquidity uses rather than financing debt. It is neither reported nor covenant debt. Leverage is 6.56x ordinary / 5.99x As Defined on this subtotal; no quality-adjusted multiple can be certified. Source-supported historical analysis is usable with restrictions, not a full model-publication or investment conclusion.

rows.label: Credit read-through, contrary evidence and monitoring — paragraph 1

cells.text: Issuer-specific transmission is two-sided. Repeated acquisitions require integration cash and inventory purchase-accounting adjustments; stock/deferred compensation is ongoing remuneration even when current expense is noncash; serial refinancing creates repeated transaction costs. A53 and A142 establish these categories and their recurrence, while A52 explicitly acknowledges excluded integration cash. Accepting all adjustments as expendable costs would overstate retained debt-service resources. Ordinary EBITDA is a transparent sensitivity, not a validated quality floor: it retains gains and does not settle the mixed Other category. Q12's negative Other removes net income effects rather than simply adding costs; do not reverse its sign or manufacture a positive add-back.

rows.label: Credit read-through, contrary evidence and monitoring — paragraph 2

cells.text: The strongest contrary evidence is genuine reported operating improvement and positive cash generation: CP-1B records revenue 2,006 versus 1,789, As Defined EBITDA 1,061 versus 912 and OCF 752 versus 636. Noncash purchase-accounting charges can be separable from current operating cash, and a documented finite refinancing or integration event may merit normalisation despite recurrence of the category. That case would win only with component-level cash/noncash detail, completed actions, finite cost tails and observed post-integration cash margins—not merely the reconciliation. No prospective synergy or run-rate saving is supplied; none is invented.

rows.label: Credit read-through, contrary evidence and monitoring — paragraph 3

cells.text: Cash quality also matters more than the modest quantified debt uplift. CP-1B's current OCF includes an accrued-interest cash source of 201, compared with cash interest paid 162 and expense 378. Dividends/equivalents of (4,396) and repurchases (316) coexist with positive OCF and September-to-December cash contraction of (3,802). Do not infer that timing-supported quarterly conversion finances repeated extraction sustainably. Annual interest and tax bridge quantities differ from cash paid; the annual test below does not deduct them twice.

rows.label: Credit read-through, contrary evidence and monitoring — paragraph 4

cells.text: Causal downside: weaker defense/aftermarket demand or delayed acquisition integration first reduces operating absorption and cash margins; persistent compensation/integration costs then fail to disappear, while delayed interest/tax payments fall due. Further shareholder payouts would reduce the cash buffer before earnings alone signal distress. A fully drawn securitization increases refinancing dependence approaching its historical July 11, 2025 expiry (CP-1B); this is not evidence of a subsequent default or renewal. Monitor component-level realised integration costs, compensation settlements, organic margins, cash interest/taxes, restrictions and distributions. Pension funding is a counterweight: A135 says FY2025 expected funding is not material; gross accounting liability is not an immediate contribution call. Observable triggers are renewed integration charges after claimed completion, cash conversion weakening as accruals settle, remediation reserve revisions, and funding/lease commitments outside the quantified subtotal. No unsupported stress magnitude or haircut is applied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Issuer-specific transmission is two-sided. Repeated acquisitions require integration cash and inventory purchase-accounting adjustments; stock/deferred compensation is ongoing remuneration even when current expense is noncash; serial refinancing creates repeated transaction costs. A53 and A142 establish these categories and their recurrence, while A52 explicitly acknowledges excluded integration cash. Accepting all adjustments as expendable costs would overstate retained debt-service resources. Ordinary EBITDA is a transparent sensitivity, not a validated quality floor: it retains gains and does not settle the mixed Other category. Q12's negative Other removes net income effects rather than simply adding costs; do not reverse its sign or manufacture a positive add-back.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest contrary evidence is genuine reported operating improvement and positive cash generation: CP-1B records revenue 2,006 versus 1,789, As Defined EBITDA 1,061 versus 912 and OCF 752 versus 636. Noncash purchase-accounting charges can be separable from current operating cash, and a documented finite refinancing or integration event may merit normalisation despite recurrence of the category. That case would win only with component-level cash/noncash detail, completed actions, finite cost tails and observed post-integration cash margins—not merely the reconciliation. No prospective synergy or run-rate saving is supplied; none is invented.

fields.value: Causal downside: weaker defense/aftermarket demand or delayed acquisition integration first reduces operating absorption and cash margins; persistent compensation/integration costs then fail to disappear, while delayed interest/tax payments fall due. Further shareholder payouts would reduce the cash buffer before earnings alone signal distress. A fully drawn securitization increases refinancing dependence approaching its historical July 11, 2025 expiry (CP-1B); this is not evidence of a subsequent default or renewal. Monitor component-level realised integration costs, compensation settlements, organic margins, cash interest/taxes, restrictions and distributions. Pension funding is a counterweight: A135 says FY2025 expected funding is not material; gross accounting liability is not an immediate contribution call. Observable triggers are renewed integration charges after claimed completion, cash conversion weakening as accruals settle, remediation reserve revisions, and funding/lease commitments outside the quantified subtotal. No unsupported stress magnitude or haircut is applied.
